text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Moslem chairman of collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic attends army parade and says that thanks to the military there was some justice for Bosnians in the peace agreement that was signed.

- Total expenses for the Pope's visit to Sarajevo were 4.3 million German marks ($2.5 million) out of which 3.3 million ($1.9 million) was covered by Moslem-Croat federation and the rest by the Sarajevo canton government.
- An average salary in the Moslem-Croat federation in the month of February this year was 244 German marks ($140), federation officials say.
- Representatives of a Japanese company donate mineral fertilizer worth $1.7 million to Moslem-Croat federation.

- Bosnia-Herzegovina will not disintegrate and there will be no further divisions apart from those that happened during the war, says Colum Murphy, spokesman for international High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt.
- Implementation of the peace agreement in Bosnia is an extremely dificult task but it has not been unsuccessful so far, outgoing U.S. envoy John Kornblum says.
- By pursuing a separatist policy, Bosnian Serb republic authorities are digging a grave for their economic development, says Robert Gelbard, newly-appointed U.S. envoy to the Balkans.

- After a difficult period at the beginning of this year better days have come to Mostar, says Martin Garrod, chief of the office of the High Representative in the town. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
